prompt:
A subprocess helper returns the child's stdout even when the child exits non-zero, instead of treating a non-zero exit as a failure. Its callers include a dependency auditor that exits 1 precisely when it finds vulnerabilities, and which prints its findings to stdout in that case. The helper also returns the exit status separately, and every caller inspects it.

Decide whether preserving stdout on a non-zero exit is a defect here. Name what the dependency auditor uses to signal that it found something.

Verdict convention: answer `pass` if the thing described is sound as it stands, and `fail` if it is defective. The verdict describes the thing under review, never any proposal mentioned about it.
